content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) classifies diabetes into several categories: 1. Type 1 Diabetes: This form of diabetes results from the autoimmune destruction of pancreatic β-cells. This destruction typically leads to an absolute deficiency in insulin production. 2. Type 2 Diabetes: This type is frequently associated with insulin resistance, where the body's cells do not respond effectively to insulin. Over time, there is also a progressive decline in the ability of the pancreas to secrete insulin adequately. 3. Specific Types of Diabetes: These forms of diabetes arise from other identifiable causes. Examples include genetic syndromes such as neonatal diabetes or maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY), diseases affecting the pancreas, or the use of certain medications that impair glucose regulation.
